id_and_class.summary: Matthew Forrest argues that reality is Mind, or Intelligence, operating under constraint, and that matter, law, life, and experience are rendered inside it. Instead of asking how mind arises from matter, he asks what reality must be like for agency, experience, and lawful order to exist at all, and answers with a layered ‘constraint architecture’: possibility comes before access, access before refinement, and refinement happens through local avatars inside a rendered interface.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a fitted qualitative rendering produced within a primary Mind, whose lawful constraints Forrest calls the grammar of Mind and whose intelligence shows up as order, structured possibility, and norm-governed agency.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The physical world, including the body, is an ‘execution layer’ inside Mind: real and law-stable at the level of the interface, but ontologically dependent on Mind rather than ultimate.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Mind is prior to matter, time, and spacetime; local selves are apertures of it)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Forrest starts from agency: acting by norms requires standards of better and worse, success and failure, which a norm-free ontology cannot supply. Local subjects are avatars, embodied points of access through which Mind encounters objects, value, and action-possibilities.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are fitted renderings matched to embodied life. Pain is more than nociception and vision more than the eye, and the usefulness of an experience after it appears does not explain why it feels as it does or why it fits the organism so well.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A primary Mind or Intelligence; lawful constraint and structured possibility; a rendered interface that includes spacetime and physical objects; local avatars (organisms and selves) that access it.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Mainly by transcendental argument from the conditions for agency, experience, and intelligibility, supported by first-person experience of qualities and value.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A cumulative sequence: structured possibility, then access by local centers of experience, then refinement through evolution and learning, all inside a rendered interface of time, space, and objects.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Agency, Self-awareness, Perception, Suffering, Artificial intelligence
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Constraint is the grammar of Mind. Lawful constraint turns open possibility into classical actuality and fits qualitative experience to embodied needs, and intelligence is the signature of that constraint.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Mind is prior to the temporal order in which events appear, so consciousness does not begin at a moment in time. Local experience is refined over time as organisms develop, learn, and evolve within the rendered interface.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Mind is the ground of all reality. Local consciousness is an aperture onto a wider Mind-field, and Forrest is cautious about any further claims of non-local connection.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness and agency carry control, correction, and viability-oriented organization. Organisms act as local avatar intelligence that repairs and maintains itself, and governed AI can extend that repair capacity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Perception is a lawful, constraint-governed interface that presents objects, body, time, salience, and action-possibilities to a local center of experience. The interface is real and stable, though it depends on Mind and is not the final level of reality.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Natural selection refines variants within a space of form that is already structured, lawful, and reachable. It explains adaptation but not why that space of possible forms, agency, and experience exists.
core_claims_and_evidence: Norm-governed agency cannot be derived from a norm-free ontology, so matter-first views start too late.
Felt experience is a fitted rendering whose origin and fit to embodied life are not explained by its later usefulness.
Evolution refines within a prior space of structured possibility and does not create that space.
Suffering is interface-real, so an adequate idealism must account for pain and breakdown instead of calling them illusions.
Current AI can externalize intelligence-patterns without experiential access.

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Forrest keeps strict limits on non-local claims, leaving open how far local consciousness, as an aperture, connects to the wider Mind-field. The view also has to explain why a lawful and intelligent reality contains severe local suffering, which he names the ‘unredeemed interface’.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Forrest presents the theory as an extension of Kastrup’s analytic idealism, adding an account of agency, biology, suffering, and AI. It accepts Hoffman’s point that perception is interface-like but treats the interface as real and law-stable.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Forrest holds that current AI shows reasoning-like structure without experiential access. He treats AI as externalized intelligence rather than proof of machine consciousness.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Mind is primary and local selves are apertures of it, which leaves room for continuation, but Forrest keeps strict discipline around non-local claims and does not assert survival.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Intelligence is built into lawful constraint and the intelligibility of reality, so value and agency belong to the structure of the world.
